Author: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Date:   Fri May 19 14:07:50 2023 -0500

    x86/platform/uv: UV support for sub-NUMA clustering
    
    Sub-NUMA clustering (SNC) invalidates previous assumptions of a 1:1
    relationship between blades, sockets, and nodes.  Fix these
    assumptions and build tables correctly when SNC is enabled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
    Signed-off-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerable construct in `uv_system_init_hub()` where it iterates over `for_each_possible_blade(bid)` and calls `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, uv_blade_to_node(bid))` (lines 1773-1774). If a socket is deconfigured and mapped to `SOCK_EMPTY` (0xffff), `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` returns `0xffff`, which is passed as an invalid node ID to `kzalloc_node`, causing a kernel panic. There is no validation or handling of `SOCK_EMPTY` before passing it to `kzalloc_node`.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability by changing the allocation loop in `uv_system_init_hub` from iterating over nodes (`for_each_node(nodeid)`) to iterating over blades (`for_each_possible_blade(bid)`). In the new loop, it calls `kzalloc_node(bytes, GFP_KERNEL, uv_blade_to_node(bid))` on line 1774. If a socket/blade is deconfigured, `uv_blade_to_node(bid)` returns `SOCK_EMPTY` (0xffff), which is passed directly to `kzalloc_node` without any validation, causing a kernel panic.
